requirements.subject: ent:for-statement
requirements.canonical: The traditional form of the for statement IS a counter loop.
requirements.original: The traditional form of the for statement defines a counter loop.

requirements.subject: ent:for-statement
requirements.canonical: The counter loop for statement has the syntax `for` "(" (VarInstance | Assignment) ";" BooleanExpression ";" Assignment ")" StatementBlock.
requirements.original:
for "(" ( VarInstance | Assignment ) ";" BooleanExpression ";" Assignment ")"
       StatementBlock

requirements.subject: ent:for-statement
requirements.canonical: A counter loop for statement IS composed of two assignments and a boolean expression.
requirements.original: The for statement contains two assignments and a boolean expression.

ambiguity.issue: The syntax also allows a variable declaration (VarInstance) instead of the first assignment; chosen reading: 'assignment' includes a variable declaration with initialization.
readings: The first part of a for statement header IS an assignment or a variable declaration with initialization.
The first part of a for statement header IS always an assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment
requirements.canonical: The first assignment of a counter loop for statement SHALL initialize the index variable of the loop.
requirements.original: The first assignment is necessary to initialize the index (or counter) variable of the loop.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-expression
requirements.canonical: The boolean expression of a counter loop for statement IS the termination condition of the loop.
requirements.original: The boolean expression terminates the loop and the second assignment is used to manipulate the index variable.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment
requirements.canonical: The second assignment of a counter loop for statement IS used to manipulate the index variable.
requirements.original: The boolean expression terminates the loop and the second assignment is used to manipulate the index variable.

requirements.subject: ent:index-variable
requirements.canonical: The value of the index variable of a counter loop IS increased, decreased or manipulated such that a termination criterion is reached after a certain number of iterations.
requirements.original: The value of the index variable is increased, decreased or manipulated in such a manner that after a certain number of execution loops a termination criteria is reached.

ambiguity.issue: Unclear whether this describes the intended use or requires that every for loop terminates; chosen reading: descriptive.
readings: The index variable IS typically manipulated so that the loop terminates (descriptive).
The second assignment SHALL manipulate the index variable so that the loop terminates (obligation).

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-expression
requirements.canonical: The termination criterion of a counter loop for statement SHALL be expressed by a boolean expression.
requirements.original: The termination criterion of the loop shall be expressed by a boolean expression.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-expression
requirements.canonical: The termination criterion of a counter loop for statement IS checked at the beginning of each new loop iteration.
requirements.original: It is checked at the beginning of each new loop iteration.

requirements.subject: ent:for-statement
requirements.condition: the boolean expression evaluates to true
requirements.canonical: If the termination criterion of a counter loop for statement evaluates to true, execution continues with the statement block of the for statement.
requirements.original: If it evaluates to true, the execution continues with the statement block in the for statement, if it evaluates to false, the execution continues with the statement which immediately follows the for loop.

requirements.subject: ent:for-statement
requirements.condition: the boolean expression evaluates to false
requirements.canonical: If the termination criterion of a counter loop for statement evaluates to false, execution continues with the statement immediately following the for loop.
requirements.original: If it evaluates to true, the execution continues with the statement block in the for statement, if it evaluates to false, the execution continues with the statement which immediately follows the for loop.

requirements.subject: ent:break-statement
requirements.condition: the break statement is not within an enclosed loop, alt, altstep or interleave
requirements.canonical: If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt statement, altstep or interleave statement, the for loop IS terminated.
requirements.original: If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt, alststep or interleave, then the loop is terminated, too.

ambiguity.issue: The text uses the misspelling 'alststep' instead of 'altstep'.

requirements.subject: ent:index-variable
requirements.canonical: The index variable of a counter loop MAY be declared before being used in the for statement.
requirements.original: The index variable of a for loop can be declared before being used in the for statement or can be declared and initialized in the for statement header.

requirements.subject: ent:index-variable
requirements.canonical: The index variable of a counter loop MAY be declared and initialized in the for statement header.
requirements.original: The index variable of a for loop can be declared before being used in the for statement or can be declared and initialized in the for statement header.

requirements.subject: ent:index-variable
requirements.condition: the index variable is declared and initialized in the for statement header
requirements.canonical: If the index variable is declared and initialized in the for statement header, the scope of the index variable IS limited to the loop body.
requirements.original: If the index variable is declared and initialized in the for statement header, the scope of the index variable is limited to the loop body, i.e. it is only visible inside the loop body.

ambiguity.issue: The header's boolean expression and second assignment also reference the index variable; chosen reading: the scope covers the for statement header and the loop body but nothing outside the for statement.
readings: The index variable IS visible in the for statement header and the loop body only.
The index variable IS visible only inside the loop body (statement block).

requirements.subject: ent:range-based-loop
requirements.canonical: The range-based loop IS a for statement that iterates over the elements provided by a range expression.
requirements.original: The range-based loop iterates over the elements provided by a range expression.

requirements.subject: ent:range-based-loop
requirements.canonical: The range-based loop has the syntax `for` "(" [`var` TypeOrNestedTypeDef] ValueRef `in` Expression ")" StatementBlock.
requirements.original:
for "(" [ var TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] ValueRef in Expression ")"
      StatementBlock

requirements.subject: ent:range-expression
requirements.canonical: The range expression of a range-based loop IS evaluated exactly once before the loop begins.
requirements.original: The range expression is evaluated once before beginning the loop and may be partially initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:range-expression
requirements.canonical: The range expression of a range-based loop MAY be partially initialized.
requirements.original: The range expression is evaluated once before beginning the loop and may be partially initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:range-expression
requirements.canonical: The range expression of a range-based loop SHALL evaluate to a value whose root type is record of, set of, array, octetstring, hexstring, bitstring, charstring or universal charstring.
requirements.original: The range _expression shall evaluate to a value with root type record of, set of, array, octetstring, hexstring, bitstring,_ **charstring or universal charstring.**

ambiguity.issue: The list does not include map types, but NOTE 1 and EXAMPLE 3 iterate over map keys (m.from); chosen reading: map key/value projections count as record of / set of values.
readings: The range expression SHALL be of one of the listed root types, where map key and value projections (`.from`, `.to`) are regarded as set of values.
The range expression SHALL be of one of the listed root types only, so iteration over map keys or values is not allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:range-based-loop
requirements.canonical: A range-based loop iterates over the elements of the range expression in sequential order.
requirements.original: Elements are iterated in sequential order.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.canonical: In each iteration of a range-based loop the corresponding element IS assigned to the iteration variable.
requirements.original: In each iteration the appropriate element is assigned to the iteration variable and the statement block is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:statement-block
requirements.canonical: In each iteration of a range-based loop the statement block IS executed after the element has been assigned to the iteration variable.
requirements.original: In each iteration the appropriate element is assigned to the iteration variable and the statement block is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.condition: the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header
requirements.canonical: If the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header, its scope and lifetime ARE limited to the statement block.
requirements.original: If the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header, its scope and lifetime is limited to the statement block, i.e. a new iteration variable is initialized in every iteration.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.condition: the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header
requirements.canonical: If the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header, a new iteration variable IS initialized in every iteration.
requirements.original: If the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header, its scope and lifetime is limited to the statement block, i.e. a new iteration variable is initialized in every iteration.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.condition: the iteration variable is declared outside the for statement
requirements.canonical: If the iteration variable is declared outside the for statement, its value after the execution of the loop IS that of the last iteration.
requirements.original: If the iteration variable is declared outside the for statement, after execution its value will be that of the last iteration.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.canonical: The assignment of an element to the iteration variable SHALL follow the assignment rules of clause 19.1.1.
requirements.original: The assignment to the iteration variable follows the rules specified in clause 19.1.1 with the exception that assignment of uninitialized elements is permitted.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.canonical: An uninitialized element MAY be assigned to the iteration variable of a range-based loop.
requirements.original: The assignment to the iteration variable follows the rules specified in clause 19.1.1 with the exception that assignment of uninitialized elements is permitted.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.canonical: When an uninitialized value is assigned to the iteration variable, the iteration variable IS uninitialized.
requirements.original: When an uninitialized value is assigned to the iterator variable, the iterator variable becomes uninitialized.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence uses 'iterator variable' while the rest of the clause uses 'iteration variable'.

requirements.subject: ent:map-type
requirements.canonical: The iteration order of map keys and map values IS tool dependent and IS NOT guaranteed to be the same from one iteration to the next.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: The iteration order of map keys and map values is tool dependent and is not guaranteed to be the same from one iteration to the next.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.canonical: The behaviour of a lazy or fuzzy iteration variable IS NOT specified.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The behaviour of lazy or fuzzy iteration variables is not specified and should not be used to avoid future compatibility issues.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.canonical: A lazy or fuzzy iteration variable SHOULD NOT be used, to avoid future compatibility issues.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The behaviour of lazy or fuzzy iteration variables is not specified and should not be used to avoid future compatibility issues.
